page.layout: One column of running text, full page. Below the last line, at the right, the catchword "omnia". No margin notes, page number or running head is printed. A small dash stands at the right edge of the line "comitas:", possibly a stray mark.

main_text.p: fiderium ? quod cùm à puero maximum tibi naturæ auctor Deus inoleuiffet, ne nunc quidem inter tantas, tam moleftas, tam difficiles curas & occupationes relanguit,nedum exaruerit. Accedit ad has tantas virtutes tuas, ceu inferta pulcherrima, fingularis morum comitas: quæ te omnibus bonis non minus reddit amabilem, quàm illa priora venerabilem. Et erit aliquis qui miretur tantum te gratia, tantum auctoritate apud omnes pollere ? mirarer potius, fi qui effet, qui cùm te vidiffet, cùm loquentem audiffet, non ftuperet. Equidem, vt primùm te vidi, & quæ antè fama de te acceperam, præfens maiora

page.notes: The first line is a fragment that continues from the previous page ("fiderium ?"). The last printed line reads "omnia", which is the catchword below the text and is not repeated in the text. The text in the first line "relanguit,nedum" has a missing space after the comma, as printed. A small dash stands at the right edge beside "comitas:"; it is not clearly a marginal note or reference, so I have not transcribed it as one. Some letters, notably "antè" and "quàm", are copied as they appear on the scan; the accent marks are reasonably clear but not certain.
